content: Lansoprazole is a gastrointestinal agent classified as an anti-ulcer medication. It is FDA-approved for the treatment of several conditions, including duodenal ulcer disease, erosive esophagitis, maintenance of healed erosive esophagitis, short-term treatment of active gastric ulcers, NSAID-associated gastric ulcers, gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), Zollinger-Ellison syndrome, and for the prevention of gastric ulcers. Common side effects include abdominal pain, constipation, diarrhea, nausea, and headache. For adults, the recommended dosages vary depending on the condition being treated. For active duodenal ulcers, the dose is 15 mg orally once daily for up to 4 weeks. For maintenance of healed ulcers, the dose is 15 mg orally once daily. For Helicobacter pylori infections, triple therapy includes 30 mg orally twice daily in combination with amoxicillin (1 gram twice daily) and clarithromycin (500 mg twice daily) for 10 to 14 days. Alternatively, another regimen involves 30 mg orally twice daily with metronidazole (500 mg twice daily) and clarithromycin (500 mg twice daily) for 10 to 14 days. For GERD, the dose is 30 mg orally once daily for 8 to 16 weeks, with an additional 8 weeks considered for recurrence. For Zollinger-Ellison syndrome, the dose can range from 60 mg orally once daily to 90 mg twice daily. Off-label uses of lansoprazole in adults are limited, and there is insufficient guideline-supported information for such uses. For Helicobacter pylori infections, quadruple therapy includes 30 mg orally twice daily, metronidazole (250 mg four times daily), bismuth subsalicylate (525 mg four times daily), and tetracycline (500 mg four times daily) for 10 to 14 days. For heartburn, the dose is 15 mg orally once daily for 14 days. In pediatric patients, the FDA-approved dosages depend on age and weight. For children aged 1 to 11 years weighing 30 kg or less, the dose is 15 mg orally once daily for up to 12 weeks, with the option to increase to 30 mg twice daily if symptoms persist after 2 or more weeks of treatment. For children aged 1 to 11 years weighing more than 30 kg, the dose is 30 mg orally once daily for up to 12 weeks, with the same option to increase the dose if needed. For children aged 12 years and older, the dose is 30 mg orally once daily for up to 8 weeks. Off-label uses in pediatric patients are also limited, with insufficient guideline-supported information available. Lansoprazole is contraindicated in individuals with a known allergy to the drug. It should not be used in patients experiencing difficulty swallowing, vomiting blood, or passing bloody or black stools, as these may indicate a serious condition requiring medical attention. Patients with liver disease, persistent heartburn lasting more than 3 months, or symptoms such as chest pain, unexplained weight loss, nausea, or vomiting should consult a doctor before use. Additionally, patients taking medications such as warfarin, antifungal agents, digoxin, theophylline, tacrolimus, or atazanavir should seek medical advice before starting lansoprazole. Patients should discontinue use and consult a doctor if heartburn persists or worsens, if the medication is needed for more than 14 days, or if more than one course of treatment is required every 4 months. Diarrhea may also occur and should prompt medical consultation. Pregnant or breastfeeding individuals should consult a healthcare professional before use. In case of overdose, immediate medical attention or contact with a Poison Control Center is advised. Lansoprazole should be taken once daily, preferably in the morning before eating. Capsules should be swallowed whole with water and not crushed or chewed. A 14-day course of treatment may be repeated every 4 months if necessary, but not more frequently unless directed by a doctor. For storage, the product should be kept at 20-25°C (68-77°F), away from high heat, humidity, and moisture. There is no established interaction between alcohol and lansoprazole, but patients should consult their doctor regarding the potential effects of combining alcohol with this medication.
